audit_findings.title: Full-share denominator versus partial-year H&E earnings and interest
audit_findings.magnitude: 4.7 million acquisition shares, 13.8% of the 34.090754 million denominator; five months of H&E results are absent; filed pro forma 2025 revenue was $4.912 billion versus $4.376 billion reported and pro forma pretax income was $106 million versus $1 million reported
audit_findings.mechanism: The full post-acquisition share count divides an OE anchor containing only seven months of H&E operations and acquisition financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: The assets and liabilities for H&E were recorded as of June 2, 2025 and the results of operations have been included in the Company's consolidated results of operations since that date.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, although its net direction is unresolved because the missing period includes both operating results and interest. The filed pro forma differences are large relative to the $52.1 million anchor, making the mismatch reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Replace the anchor using the first full post-acquisition fiscal year and rerun all scenarios with full-year H&E operations, interest, integration costs, synergies and the corresponding fully diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: One-time acquisition costs may be embedded permanently in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $199 million pretax, including $193 million associated with H&E; 382% of the $52.1 million anchor; exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrecurring transaction expense left in anchor OE is treated as a recurring annual cost and propagated through every forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Transaction expenses were $199 million in 2025 compared to $11 million in 2024 due to costs incurred related to the acquisition of H&E, primarily the one-time termination fee paid on behalf of H&E of $64 million, advisory fees of $27 million, commitment fees related to the Bridge Facility of $21 million, and various other financial consulting, professional and legal fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The expenses and their acquisition-related character are demonstrated, but the record does not show which amounts the OE worksheet normalized. Because the filed expense is almost four times the anchor, even a partial qualifying add-back could materially increase value.
audit_findings.action: Trace all $199 million through the OE calculation, remove only demonstrably nonrecurring items, retain recurring integration or operating costs, apply the proper tax treatment and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Cinelease creates an unrecognized shrinking-perimeter contamination
audit_findings.magnitude: $49 million pretax disposal-related loss, 94% of the $52.1 million anchor; $100 million initial consideration and $32 million earnout receivable; pre-sale operating contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor can include earnings from a divested business and disposal-related losses or gains, while retained sale consideration belongs in the equity bridge rather than recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, the Company recorded a pre-tax loss on assets held for sale of approximately $ 49 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The divestiture and loss are demonstrated, but whether the worksheet removed them and the direction of Cinelease's pre-sale operating contribution remain unresolved. The $49 million loss alone is nearly the entire anchor, so perimeter normalization is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 OE excluding Cinelease operating results, the held-for-sale loss, closing gain and earnout remeasurements; separately reconcile sale proceeds, debt repayment and any remaining earnout asset to the bridge without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Large deferred-tax claim may not be captured by the zero-tax anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.446 billion net deferred-tax liability and $24 million FY2025 cash taxes versus a $0 total tax provision; $24 million equals 46% of the $52.1 million anchor; sustainable OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Using the zero GAAP tax provision without a sustainable cash-tax adjustment can overstate OE as accelerated tax depreciation and acquired-basis differences reverse.
audit_findings.evidence: As described in Notes 2 and 15 to the consolidated financial statements, the Company has a net deferred tax liability balance of $1.4 billion as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The deferred-tax balance, zero provision and cash payments are demonstrated, but the record does not establish that $24 million is the recurring tax burden or that the OE worksheet omitted it. The observed cash-tax amount is nevertheless large enough relative to the anchor to make the issue materially valuation-sensitive.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE tax charge to current taxes, cash payments, credits, interest limitations, NOL usage and the reversal schedule for acquired fleet and intangible differences, then rerun using a sustainable cash-tax estimate.

audit_findings.title: Spin-off indemnities are unquantified claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: A crystallized indemnity would reduce OE when paid or require a separate liability deduction in the equity bridge if probable and measurable.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is responsible for a portion of these shared liabilities (typically 15 %), as set forth in that agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual 15% sharing obligation exists, but no present valuation error or measurable exposure is demonstrated. The 2025 10-K reports no material claims or expenses under the separation agreements, and the June 2026 10-Q reports no material change, so this is presently a contingent forward-looking risk.
audit_findings.action: Monitor New Hertz proceedings, indemnity notices, tax matters, guarantees and related accruals each reporting period; quantify and add a bridge liability or scenario cash outflow when an exposure becomes probable or reasonably estimable.

audit_findings.title: Cinelease earnout asset appears omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $32 million, or $0.94 per diluted share; 4.35% of the $736 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The probability-weighted non-operating receivable should be added separately to the equity bridge, while its remeasurement gains or losses should be excluded from recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The earnout receivable of $ 32 million is recorded within other long-term assets in the Company's consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2025, no adjustments to the fair value were made during the year ending December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q confirms that the $32 million receivable remains outstanding with unchanged fair value, while the stated bridge includes no corresponding asset. Adding the entire carrying value would raise the valuation range only from $17.53-$25.24 to approximately $18.47-$26.18 per share, still far below the $140.92 market price, so it does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm continued collectibility, add the risk-adjusted receivable to the bridge, exclude future fair-value movements from OE and verify that sale proceeds or debt repayments are not counted twice.
